chunks: Al-Tatarī narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān from Sulaymān ibn Khālid from Abū ʿAbd Allāh (peace be upon him)

key_terms.مِثْلُهُ: Like it / The same (referring to a previous ruling or narration)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'mithluhu' indicate in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* functions as a cross-reference (tashbih), indicating that the ruling on the Qibla is identical to the preceding narration. It highlights the meticulous chain of transmission (isnad) characteristic of Shia jurisprudence, linking Imam al-Sadiq through Sulayman ibn Khalid to ensure the authenticity of the directional prayer guidelines.
